instructions: HUMAN LABELING — one rater (one-person panel for now). For each pair open instrument/<id>.png:
the LEFT half is state A beside ITS concept, the RIGHT half is state B beside ITS concept.
Set humanLabel to which build MORE FAITHFULLY realizes ITS OWN concept image:
"A" (left more faithful), "B" (right more faithful), or "tie" (genuinely rank-either-way).
Judge the GLANCE — does the build look like its picture? — not block-level material agreement.
When done, save this file as labels.human.json in this directory; the agreement harness reads it as the GATE.

pairs.rationale: faithful rustic gatehouse (own concept) vs the same build judged against a CLASSICAL arc concept — obviously the match is more faithful.
faithful cottage (own concept) vs the same build against a GATEHOUSE concept — obvious.
faithful barn (own concept) vs the same build against a COTTAGE concept — obvious.
fully-faithful gatehouse vs the SAME build with the dark-oak roof swapped to warm spruce — clearly worse, or a plausible wood-shingle either-way? The single-factor-material contestable pair.
wrong roof MATERIAL (spruce vs dark timber) vs a MISSING dressing (unframed rectangular gate vs arched) — which partial defect costs more faithfulness? Genuinely rank-either-way.
a real-but-incomplete rustic gatehouse (gaping gate) vs a faithful build judged against a WRONG (classical) concept — does a partially-faithful gatehouse beat a fully-wrong-picture one? Contestable.
faithful half-timber cottage vs the same form with a PLAIN upper storey (missing the stud grammar) — clearly worse, or close?
a plain-but-real cottage vs a faithful cottage build against a WRONG (gatehouse) concept — does the incomplete-but-right-subject build beat the wrong-picture one? Contestable.
